  - region "Simple English explanation of Rational Functions":
    - paragraph: In simple English
    - heading "Understand Rational Functions" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "A rational function is a quotient of polynomials. (x+1)/(x−2) excludes x=2, has f(0)=−1/2, and after cancelling a common factor the original zero of the denominator still restricts the domain. A useful rule is Restriction: denominator != 0. You can learn Rational Functions by trying one small example instead of long theory."
    - paragraph: "Set the original denominator to zero, keep that restriction after any cancel, then evaluate allowed inputs. Example: Find the excluded value of (x+1)/(x-2). Set x-2=0. Solve x=2. So the answer is 2."
    - paragraph: "In real life, average cost: Cost per item can be a rational function. Watch out: Cancelling and allowing a forbidden x-value. Keep every original denominator restriction."
    - complementary:
      - generic: Try this example
      - paragraph: Find the excluded value of (x+1)/(x-2).
      - generic "Compare your answer"
